shortlist.title: SuperSNEC: Fast and Accurate Light-curve Production for Large Hydrodynamic Model Grids Using Adaptive Gridding
shortlist.abstract: We present SuperSNEC, an accelerated version of the SuperNova Explosion Code (SNEC) designed for rapid production of large radiation-hydrodynamic model grids using low-zone-count simulations (∼100 zones). The main advance is adaptive gridding of the computational grid, which preserves light-curve fidelity relative to a high-resolution SNEC baseline (∼1000 zones) while delivering a runtime improvement of ∼420 × . SuperSNEC also includes solver optimizations, optimized radioactive-energy deposition and ray-tracing, and improved 56 Ni mixing controls. We quantify the speed-accuracy trade-off for a 100-zone configuration against a 1000-zone reference and define baseline settings for efficient large-grid inference of stripped-envelope supernovae. Our optimized 100-zone setup achieves an rms light-curve residual of 0.022 mag relative to the 1000-zone reference, at a runtime of < 2 s per model. Applied to SN 2011dh (Type IIb), SN 1993J (Type IIb), and SN 2020oi (Type Ic), SuperSNEC recovers light-curve parameters consistent with the literature. In particular, SN 2020oi is well reproduced by a model powered by 56 Ni decay and the standard hydrodynamic evolution, with no clear evidence that an additional power source such as interaction with circumstellar meterial or a central engine is required.

shortlist.title: Environmental Dependence of Galaxy Properties in the Southern GAMA Regions
shortlist.abstract: Using data from the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) survey, we investigate how galaxy properties correlate with the local environment, focusing on its two southern regions (G02 and G23) that have not previously been examined in this context. We employ two-point and marked correlation functions to quantify the environmental dependence of galaxy color, stellar mass, luminosity across the u , g , r , J , and K bands, as well as star formation rate (SFR) and specific star formation rate (sSFR). Our results show that u − r and g − r colors are most strongly correlated with local overdensity, followed by stellar mass. The SFR and sSFR exhibit a clear inverse relationship with environmental density, consistent with the trend observed for u -band luminosity, which traces young stellar populations. The galaxies brighter in the g , J , and K bands preferentially inhabit denser regions. We interpret the environmental dependence of color using halo occupation distribution (HOD) modeling. The HOD modeling indicates that red galaxies trace dense environments more strongly than blue galaxies, exhibiting significantly higher satellite fractions and occupying more massive halos. We demonstrate that both redshift and stellar mass incompleteness systematically affect clustering measurements, generally enhancing the observed environmental dependence. Comparing our measurements from the southern regions with those from the equatorial GAMA regions, we find that the overall environmental trends remain consistent. The measured correlations provide key constraints for models of galaxy assembly across mass and environment, while environmental trends in color and near-infrared luminosity trace stellar mass growth and quenching with redshift.

shortlist.title: Helios: Real Real-Time Long Video Generation Model
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: We introduce Helios, the first 14B video generation model that runs at 19.5 FPS on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU and supports minute-scale generation while matching the quality of a strong baseline. We make breakthroughs along three key dimensions: (1) robustness to long-video drifting without commonly used anti-drifting heuristics such as self-forcing, errorbanks, or keyframe sampling; (2) real-time generation without standard acceleration techniques such as KV-cache, sparse/linear attention, or quantization; and (3) training without parallelism or sharding frameworks, enabling image-diffusion-scale batch sizes while fitting up to four 14B models within 80 GB of GPU memory. Specifically, Helios is a 14B autoregressive diffusion model with a unified input representation that natively supports T2V, I2V, and V2V tasks. To mitigate drifting in long-video generation, we characterize typical failure modes and propose simple yet effective training strategies that explicitly simulate drifting during training, while eliminating repetitive motion at its source. For efficiency, we heavily compress the historical and noisy context and reduce the number of sampling steps, yielding computational costs comparable to or even lower than those of 1.3B video generative models. Moreover, we introduce infrastructure-level optimizations that accelerate both inference and training while reducing memory consumption. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Helios consistently outperforms prior methods on both short- and long-video generation. We release the training and inference code and model checkpoints to support further development by the community.

shortlist.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
shortlist.abstract: Rings are ubiquitous among the giant planets in the solar system, yet their presence around exoplanets remains observationally unconstrained. As direct imaging missions such as the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope approach first light, understanding the influence of circumplanetary rings on reflected light photometry is critical for the accurate interpretation and follow-up of direct imaging observations. We present a hybrid forward model for reflected light phase curves of ringed exoplanets, coupling a ray-casting framework for computing mutual planet–ring shadowing with empirical reflectance spectra from Cassini observations of Saturn’s rings. We model Jupiter-like planets with opaque, icy rings spanning 1–10× the radial extent of Saturn’s A, B, and C rings across a grid of inclinations and ring obliquities. Our simulations show that rings enhance the flux ratios at favorable ring geometries. Saturn-equivalent rings increase peak flux by a factor of 3.1 in the visible, while more extended rings produce enhanced contrasts exceeding an order of magnitude. The flux contribution of a ring is highly sensitive to obliquity and orbital location. At certain geometries, rings can suppress total system brightness below that of a ringless planet. We highlight multiband observations as a complementary route for diagnosing the presence of an exoring. We also apply the model to υ Andromedae d as an observational test case and discuss the implications for exoring detectability with the Roman Coronagraph. Exorings have the potential to bias inferred planetary properties from direct images and must be properly accounted for in observation preparation and interpretation.

shortlist.abstract: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O 2 ) and CO 2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year −1 decade −1 ) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year −1 ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year −1 , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

shortlist.title: Generating interesting scientific ideas using knowledge graphs and LLMs: Evaluations with 100 research group leaders
shortlist.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
shortlist.abstract: The rapid growth of scientific literature makes it increasingly challenging for researchers to identify novel and impactful ideas, especially across disciplines. Modern AI systems offer new opportunities for scientific ideation, but how compelling are AI-generated ideas, and how can their quality be improved? Here, we introduce SCIMUSE , which generates personalized research ideas using a knowledge graph of 58 million papers and a large language model (LLM). A central focus of this work is to understand how interesting these ideas are. Therefore, we conducted a large-scale evaluation in which more than 100 research group leaders—spanning the natural sciences to the humanities—rated over 4,400 personalized ideas according to their level of interest. Overall, expert ratings were modest (mean 2.40 on a 5-point scale, most common rating 1), while 24.9% of ideas were rated 4 or 5. We find that supplying concept pairs selected using the knowledge graph does not improve expert-rated interest over a titles-only GPT baseline. High-citation-predicted pairs even showed a weak tendency (1.94 σ ) toward lower interest than random pairs. Nevertheless, graph features can be used to control properties of ideas, and, using this unique evaluation dataset, we show that idea interest can be predicted with both a supervised neural network based on graph features and a zero-shot ranking approach based on an LLM. Our work provides an AI methodology for generating scientific ideas and a large-scale interdisciplinary expert evaluation, paving the way to study and improve difficult-to-measure metrics such as expert-perceived scientific interestingness.

shortlist.title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA)
shortlist.abstract: The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA, https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/ ) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent TP53 , PIK3CA , PTEN , SETD2 , MAP3K14 , and FAT4 alterations; copy number events included MYC amplifications and PTEN deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.

shortlist.title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
shortlist.abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

shortlist.title: Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a)
shortlist.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). However, the effect of pelacarsen on cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted an international, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease and a lipoprotein(a) level of at least 70 mg per deciliter. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous pelacarsen (80 mg) administered monthly or matching placebo. The primary end point was a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 8350 patients underwent randomization, with 8322 included in the efficacy analysis; 4157 patients were assigned to receive pelacarsen, and 4165 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 59.7 years, and 27.0% were women. The median lipoprotein(a) level at baseline was 236 nmol per liter. At 12 months, the lipoprotein(a) level was 64.4 nmol per liter in the pelacarsen group and 233.4 nmol per liter in the placebo group. The median follow-up was 4.7 years. A primary end-point event occurred in 511 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 503 (12.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.15, P = 0.76). Among patients with a baseline lipoprotein(a) level of at least 90 mg per deciliter, a primary end-point event occurred in 402 of 3266 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 403 of 3274 (12.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15; P = 0.99). shortlist.title: Decyanation, Dioxygenation, and Oxidative Ring Contraction Catalyzed by the DUF4243 Oxidase OzmD Rely on Ferric Oxygen Activation
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Domain of unknown function 4243 (DUF4243) family proteins are an emerging class of nonheme mononuclear iron enzymes characterized by a distinctive iron-binding motif comprised of four histidine (His) and one Nε-carboxylysine (Kcx) residue. Although predominantly found in fungi, OzmD is the only characterized bacterial member. OzmD catalyzes oxidative rearrangement of an aminopyridone ring into a 1,3-oxazine moiety with concomitant cyanide elimination in the final step of oxazinomycin biosynthesis. Herein, the X-ray crystal structure of OzmD is solved, demonstrating the presence of a conserved 4-His-1-Kcx iron-binding motif similar to other DUF4243 family proteins. Biochemical characterization using a substrate analog carrying a hydroxypyridone ring reveals that OzmD also exhibits intrinsic dioxygenase activity, catalyzing a transformation analogous to those of fungal DUF4243 dioxygenases. Electron paramagnetic resonance and Mössbauer spectroscopic characterization of MinCC, a functionally equivalent homologue of OzmD, reveals that the as-isolated protein predominantly contains ferric iron, which can be reduced to the ferrous state upon binding with either the native substrate or the hydroxy analog under anaerobic conditions. These findings support a unified mechanism in which catalysis begins with single-electron transfer from the substrate to ferric iron, enabling molecular oxygen activation and formation of an alkylperoxide intermediate. Overall reaction mechanisms for substrates bearing aminopyridone and hydroxypyridone rings are proposed based on chemical precedents and computational analyses. These findings reveal that OzmD employs a distinctive FeIII-dependent path for oxygen activation in contrast to the classical FeII-dependent route used by most oxygenases…

shortlist.title: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.

shortlist.title: Operando pH Measurements of OER within a Porous Oxygen-Evolving Electrode
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Three-dimensional porous electrodes, such as those in membrane electrode assemblies, are widely employed in electrochemical devices due to their high surface area and achievable current density. The heterogeneous internal structure of the porous electrode microenvironment engenders local concentration gradients owing to mass transport constraints. Localized microenvironments with properties distinct from those of the bulk solution are especially prevalent for electrocatalytic reactions that produce or consume protons, as local basic or acidic environments may significantly influence the energy efficiency and selectivity of proton-coupled electron transfer reactions that are necessary for small-molecule activation. Here, we develop an operando method employing polymer-bound fluorescent sensors (PFS) to directly quantify local pH and the internal proton gradient in a porous electrode for the oxygen evolution reaction catalyzed by IrOx supported on indium-tin oxide (ITO). The PFS uncovers notable pH gradients within a 3-μm-thick layer of the OER electrode in unbuffered electrolyte, even at low current density. Proton transport dynamics were found to be influenced significantly by the proton adsorption properties of the ITO support, revealing a previously unrecognized role of the oxide support in modifying the local pH gradient. The PFS method should prove useful in the study and evaluation of electrochemical devices, including fuel cells, bipolar and other ion-conducting membranes, and electrolyzers.

shortlist.title: Electrostatic Presolvation Enables Selectivity in Photoinduced Ligand Exchange
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Functional group compatibility remains a central challenge in photochemical C–H activation with metal complexes. Strongly donating groups preferentially coordinate to the reactive unsaturated metal and suppress weaker C–H coordination and σ-complex formation required for C–H bond activation. Controlling the initial coordination in photoinduced ligand exchange is therefore one approach to achieving selectivity in bond activation. Here, we resolve the elementary steps of photoinduced CO to acetonitrile ligand substitution for Rh(acac)(CO)2 with femtosecond-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Rh L3-edge. We directly observe the formation of a hitherto undetected transient acetonitrile C–H σ-complex and its subsequent rearrangement to the thermodynamically favored nitrogen-coordinated solvent complex. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the initial C–H coordination is enabled by electrostatic presolvation, which orients the acetonitrile methyl groups toward the metal center prior to CO dissociation. Our results point to a general strategy to direct selectivity in C–H activation by controlling coordination through presolvation.

shortlist.title: Private debt versus bank debt in corporate borrowing
shortlist.abstract: Using administrative bank loan-level data matched to private debt deals, we study the interaction between private and bank debt for a large segment of dual borrowers. These firms use private debt for investment and bank credit lines for liquidity insurance. Private debt carries higher spreads and commonly features flexible, equity-like terms that are associated with greater reliance on bank credit lines. Relative to bank-only borrowers, dual borrowers obtain more and larger credit lines and draw them more intensively following liquidity shocks. Our findings suggest that private debt substitutes for bank term loans but complements banks’ provision of credit lines.

shortlist.title: MOFs for photonics: bridging photocatalysis, optical wireless communication, and high-energy radiation sensing
shortlist.abstract: Light-conversion materials hold considerable promise for addressing global energy and environmental challenges, with applications spanning photocatalysis, optical wireless communication (OWC), and high-energy photon detection and imaging. However, conventional light-conversion materials often suffer from limited conversion efficiency, demanding synthesis conditions, poor stability, and environmental toxicity, hindering their large-scale deployment and long-term sustainability. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), assembled from metal nodes and organic linkers, have emerged as a distinctive class of hybrid materials that integrate the complementary advantages of inorganic and organic components. Their structural and compositional tunability, high surface areas, and tailorable electronic and photophysical properties provide exceptional opportunities for regulating photon absorption, emission, and energy transfer across a broad energy range. This review highlights recent advances over the past five years in MOF-based light-conversion systems for photocatalysis, OWC, and X-ray imaging. Particular emphasis is placed on how the rational design of metal nodes, organic linkers, framework structures, and guest components governs light harvesting, excited-state dynamics, and luminescence properties. We further discuss energy-transfer engineering within MOFs and across MOF-guest interfaces, elucidating its critical role in directing excitation energy, accelerating radiative processes, and improving photon-conversion efficiency. By establishing relationships among framework structure, energy-transfer pathways, and functional performance, this review provides design principles for next-generation MOF platforms toward efficient solar-to-chemical conversion, ultrafast OWC, and…

shortlist.title: Non-carbon-supported low-loading precious metals: from rational synthesis to mechanism insight for advanced electrocatalysis
shortlist.abstract: Non-carbon-supported low-loading precious-metal (NCS-LLPM) electrocatalysts address the cost and scarcity bottlenecks inherent in precious metals through their ultralow loading, rendering scale-up economically viable. Their combined activity and durability meet device-level operational requirements and facilitate the laboratory-to-device transition toward industrial electrolyzers. Scaled deployment in clean electrochemical conversion curtails reliance on fossil-derived processes, offering a tangible route to emission reduction and sustainability. Rational design of non-carbon supports exploits their diverse bonding modes and coordination configurations with metal sites, which constitute structural degrees of freedom largely absent in conventional carbon supports. This bonding drives charge transfer and orbital hybridization, reshaping the electronic structure of the anchored metal and tightening the metal-support interaction. These reinforced interactions also suppress the oxidative corrosion and agglomeration that typically degrade carbon-supported catalysts, improving long-term operational stability. This review first summarizes typical synthetic routes and highlights advanced strategies including microwave-assisted fabrication and high-throughput screening. The role of non-carbon supports in regulating catalytic performance is examined in terms of electronic structure modulation, conductivity enhancement, and coordination-environment optimization. It further categorizes reported NCS-LLPM catalysts, including emerging single-atom systems, and summarizes recent advances across key energy conversion reactions, such as hydrogen evolution, oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, nitrate reduction, alcohol oxidation, and carbon dioxide reduction. shortlist.abstract: A single dose of an siRNA targeting liver expression of CIDEB was associated with a reduction in liver fat of 58 to 80% at week 36 after treatment in persons with metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease.

shortlist.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
shortlist.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. RESULTS: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. shortlist.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
shortlist.abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation's largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non-Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. shortlist.title: What’s at Stake? Understanding the Role of Home Equity in Flood Insurance Demand
shortlist.abstract: Changing flood insurance demand shifts climate risk across homeowners, lenders, and governments. We show that flood insurance take-up follows rising and falling home equity over the housing boom and bust across markets with different price dynamics. To isolate the causal effect of risk shifting on insurance demand, we study flood insurance policy renewals over the housing bust, exploiting granular differences in purchase timing that led policyholders to experience differential changes in skin-in-the-game exposure to flood risk for the same change in home equity. When homeowners have less equity exposure to flood losses, they are less likely to renew their policies. Lenders, in turn, have little incentive to require flood insurance when they can sell their mortgages to federally backed mortgage purchasers. This paper was accepted by Tomasz Piskorski, finance. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.01302 .

shortlist.title: Person Recognition at Altitude and Range: Fusion of Face, Body Shape and Gait
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: We address the problem of whole-body person recognition in unconstrained environments. This problem arises in surveillance scenarios such as those in the IARPA Biometric Recognition and Identification at Altitude and Range (BRIAR) program, where biometric data is captured at long standoff distances, elevated viewing angles, and under adverse atmospheric conditions (e.g., turbulence and high wind velocity). To this end, we propose FarSight, a unified end-to-end system for person recognition that integrates complementary biometric cues across face, gait, and body shape modalities. FarSight comprises four core modules: multi-subject detection and tracking, recognition-aware video restoration, modality-specific biometric feature encoding, and quality-guided multi-modal fusion. Rather than treating these modules as independent processing stages, FarSight coordinates key stage-level decisions around the final biometric objective: tracking maintains identity-consistent temporal evidence, restoration is selectively invoked and optimized for recognition, and modality-quality estimates guide score fusion. This coordinated design supports recognition under degraded image conditions, large pose and scale variations, and cross-domain gaps. Extensive experiments on the BRIAR dataset, one of the most comprehensive benchmarks for long-range, multi-modal biometric recognition, demonstrate the effectiveness of FarSight. Compared with our preliminary system [1] on the Face-Included treatment set of BRIAR EVP 5.0.1, the current system improves 1:1 verification (TAR@0.1% FAR) by 34.4 percentage points and closed-set identification (Rank-20) by 17.8 percentage points, while reducing open-set identification errors (FNIR@1% FPIR) by 34.3 percentage points. shortlist.title: An (in)complete NIRSpec census of Balmer absorption in Type 1 AGN – radiation-driven outflows in little red dots, quasars and variable stars
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: A notable achievement of the first generation of JWST surveys was the discovery of an abundance of faint high-redshift (z > 4) broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the Lbol < 1045 erg s−1 regime, previously only accessible at z < 1. The high prevalence of absorption features in their broad hydrogen lines is one of the peculiarities of a significant fraction of this new population. In this paper, we conduct a broad census of Balmer absorption in a sample of 47 Type-1 AGN spanning 2 < z < 7. Accounting for incompleteness of JWST spectroscopic data, we estimate that 44₋₆⁺²¹ % of Little Red Dots (LRDs) have absorption in Hα while the incidence rate is <25 % (at 2σ) in Little Blue Dots (LBDs). Additionally, R1000 JWST/NIRSpec data is strongly resolution limited, implying an inability to disentangle Doppler broadening in the absorption from optical depth effects. This is alleviated with R2700 observations, although some degeneracies remain. We find a significant correlation between the velocity of the Balmer absorption and the [OIII]5007 narrow line luminosity, suggesting a common driving mechanism. We do not find any other significant correlations (and do not confirm previously claimed correlations) between Balmer absorption and other spectral properties of LRDs (except for the expected correlation between Hα and Hβ absorption velocities). Comparing LRDs, quasars and stellar Hα absorbers, we establish that absorption in both LRDs and broad absorption line quasars is consistent with radiatively driven outflows, echoing the physics of variable stars yet occurring at vastly different scales.

shortlist.title: The Huang–Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
shortlist.abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin 1/2 1 / 2 fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.

shortlist.title: Shadow banks on the rise: Evidence across market segments
shortlist.abstract: This paper examines the comparative advantages of shadow banks across market segments. Combining credit bureau data on retail loans in India with weather shocks as a proxy for credit demand, we show that Fintechs respond more in uncollateralized markets. In contrast, non-Fintech shadow banks exhibit stronger responsiveness in collateralized markets. Exploiting geographic heterogeneity in the adoption of digital payments, we identify technology as the key advantage for Fintechs. Leveraging four natural experiments, we document the significance of lower regulation for non-Fintech shadow banks. Our results suggest that the comparative advantage of shadow banks differs across market segments.

shortlist.title: Rethinking Distribution Shifts: Empirical Analysis and Modeling for Tabular Data
shortlist.abstract: Different distribution shifts require different interventions, and algorithms must be grounded in the specific shifts they address. However, methodological development for robust algorithms typically relies on structural assumptions that lack empirical validation. Advocating for an empirically grounded data-driven approach to algorithm development, we build an empirical testbed comprising natural shifts across 8 tabular data sets, 172 distribution pairs over 45 methods, and 90,000 method configurations encompassing empirical risk minimization and distributionally robust optimization (DRO) methods. We find that Y|X-shifts are most prevalent in our testbed, in stark contrast to the heavy focus on X (covariate)-shifts in the machine learning literature, and that the performance of robust algorithms is no better than that of vanilla methods. To understand why, we conduct an in-depth empirical analysis of DRO methods and find that underlooked implementation details—such as the choice of underlying model class (e.g., LightGBM) and hyperparameter selection—have a bigger impact on performance than the ambiguity set or its radius. We illustrate via case studies how a data-driven understanding of distribution shifts can provide a new approach to algorithm development. This paper was accepted by Wolfram Wiesemann, data science. shortlist.title: Urban Architect: Steerable 3D Driving Scene Generation With Layout Prior
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: Text-to-3D generation has achieved remarkable success via large-scale text-to-image diffusion models. Nevertheless, scaling this methodology to large-scale driving scenes is underexplored. Driving scenes, characterized by numerous elements, intricate arrangement relationships, and vast scale, present a formidable barrier to the interpretability of ambiguous textual descriptions for effective model optimization. In this work, we surmount the limitations by introducing a compositional 3D layout representation into text-to-3D paradigm, serving as an additional prior. It comprises a set of semantic primitives with simple geometric structures and explicit arrangement relationships, complementing textual descriptions and enabling steerable generation. Specifically, we represent the scene via 2D Gaussian splatting and develop two innovative optimization strategies: (1) Layout-Guided Variational Score Distillation, which addresses model optimization inadequacies by conditioning the score distillation sampling process with geometric and semantic constraints of 3D layouts; (2) Semantic-Depth Score Distillation Sampling, which ensures alignment of semantics, geometry, and appearance by matching the rendered semantic and depth maps with 3D layouts. Extensive experiments substantiate the capability of our framework to scale text-to-3D generation to large-scale driving scenes that cover over 1000 m driving distance for the first time. We also present various scene editing demonstrations, showing the powers of steerable urban scene generation.

shortlist.title: Optimization Problems with Nonconvexities Involving the Euclidean Norm: Challenges, Progress, and Opportunities
shortlist.abstract: The field of global optimization has advanced significantly over the past three decades, yet the solution to global optimality of even small instances of many optimization problems with nonconvexities involving the Euclidean norm remains beyond the reach of modern global optimization methods. These problems include numerous well-known and high-impact open research questions from a diverse collection of both fundamental and applied fields of science and engineering. In this review, we survey applications in which these problems arise, describe sources of computational intractability, summarize existing solution methods, and identify promising research directions for future work. We also introduce EuclidLib, a library of instances of optimization problems of this type, to aid in performance benchmarking and algorithm development. The solution to global optimality of all problems in EuclidLib would represent a significant achievement for the field of global optimization and an important contribution to mathematics, science, and engineering.

shortlist.title: Tackling the Commercial Determinants of Obesity: A Review of Key Policies and Strategies
shortlist.abstract: A growing body of evidence demonstrates that commercial entities play an important role in shaping the prevalence, incidence, and distribution of obesity. This narrative review examines policy solutions to address the commercial determinants of obesity. We describe how five business sectors (food, beverages, and agriculture; media and entertainment; sports and recreation; transportation; and medical care and pharmaceuticals) shape obesity prevalence through three key behavioral pathways: diet, physical activity, and use of medical care. We then examine four categories of tools available to national and subnational governments to address the commercial determinants: legal and regulatory measures, fiscal policies, market governance mechanisms, and litigation. Finally, we discuss three strategies that can support the successful implementation of these measures: building cross-sectoral support, limiting undue influence in policymaking processes, and designing policies informed by precedent and designed to withstand challenges. We conclude by highlighting key insights for policymakers seeking to make measurable progress in preventing and reducing obesity.

shortlist.title: Labor Unions and Better Health
shortlist.abstract: Social-class inequities in health arise from power imbalances in our political-economic system. However, through labor-union organizing, workers can build power to improve their life chances and health. In our review, we describe the rich historical, theoretical, and mechanistic evidence linking unions and health and critically evaluate the state of quantitative research on the topic. Most individual-level and ecological studies have estimated small beneficial or null union-health associations. However, as we describe, the studies are limited in number, particularly outside the Global North, and face many technical and conceptual challenges, including feedback loops between unions and societies' political-economic contexts. We conclude with recommendations for enhancing the rigor and utility of union-health research, including by richly contextualizing studies' findings and by answering questions raised by workers themselves. As social and economic inequities intensify and workers face heightening attacks on their well-being, unions remain crucial organizations for advancing health justice.

shortlist.title: RAD-2: Scaling Reinforcement Learning in a Generator-Discriminator Framework
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: High-level autonomous driving requires motion planners capable of modeling multimodal future uncertainties while remaining robust in closed-loop interactions. Although diffusion-based planners are effective at modeling complex trajectory distributions, they often suffer from stochastic instabilities and the lack of corrective negative feedback when trained purely with imitation learning. To address these issues, we propose RAD-2, a unified generator-discriminator framework for closed-loop planning. Specifically, a diffusion-based generator is used to produce diverse trajectory candidates, while an RL-optimized discriminator reranks these candidates according to their long-term driving quality. This decoupled design avoids directly applying sparse scalar rewards to the full high-dimensional trajectory space, thereby improving optimization stability. To further enhance reinforcement learning, we introduce Temporally Consistent Group Relative Policy Optimization, which exploits temporal coherence to alleviate the credit assignment problem. In addition, we propose On-policy Generator Optimization, which converts closed-loop feedback into structured longitudinal optimization signals and progressively shifts the generator toward high-reward trajectory manifolds. To support efficient large-scale training, we introduce BEV-Warp, a high- throughput simulation environment that performs closed-loop evaluation directly in Bird's-Eye View feature space via spatial warping. RAD-2 reduces the collision rate by 56% compared with strong diffusion-based planners. Preliminary real-world mainpaper validation on four routes across two cities further indicates improved perceived safety and driving smoothness in complex urban traffic. shortlist.title: The Data-Driven Censored Newsvendor Problem
shortlist.abstract: We study a censored variant of the data-driven newsvendor problem, where the decision maker must select an ordering quantity that minimizes expected overage and underage costs based only on offline censored sales data rather than historical demand realizations. Our goal is to understand how the degree of historical demand censoring affects the performance of any learning algorithm for this problem. To isolate this impact, we adopt a distributionally robust optimization framework, evaluating policies according to their worst-case regret over an ambiguity set of distributions. This set is defined by the largest historical order quantity (the observable boundary of the data set), and contains all distributions matching the true demand distribution up to this boundary while allowing them to be arbitrary afterward. We demonstrate a spectrum of achievability under demand censoring by deriving a natural necessary and sufficient condition under which vanishing regret is an achievable goal. In regimes in which it is not, we exactly characterize the information loss due to censoring: an insurmountable lower bound on the performance of any policy, even when the decision maker has access to infinitely many demand samples. We then leverage these sharp characterizations to propose a natural robust algorithm that adapts to the historical level of demand censoring. We derive finite-sample guarantees for this algorithm across all possible censoring regimes and show its near-optimality with matching lower bounds (up to polylogarithmic factors). We moreover demonstrate its robust performance via extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world data sets. This paper was accepted by Wolfram Wiesemann, data science. shortlist.title: Hi intensity mapping with MeerKAT: A measurement of the 21-cm auto-spectrum on cosmological scales
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: We report a direct measurement of the 21-cm signal from neutral hydrogen (Hi) via the intensity mapping technique at redshift z = 0.42 through its power spectrum at cosmological scales 0.095 h Mpc−1 < k < 0.245 h Mpc−1. We analyse intensity maps observed in the frequency range 971.2 MHz < ν < 1023.6 MHz during the 2021 observational campaign of the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) spanning an area of approximately 236 °2. Capitalising on the depth of this survey, we divide the data set into multiple observationally independent subsets. After performing blind contaminant separation independently on each subset, we exploit internal cross-correlations to suppress the instrumental noise plateau and isolate the cosmological signal from residual systematics. Although the subsets’ auto-spectra show the presence of excess power that we deem linked to still unresolved systematics, the cross-spectra measurements satisfactorily pass a battery of null and robustness tests. We introduce a multi-subset formalism to infer the amplitude of the Hi auto-spectrum from our internal cross-spectra measurements while marginalising the potential signal loss that occurs during data processing, reaching a detection with signal-to-noise ratio of 6.2. We constrain the clustering amplitude of the signal in terms of the Hi cosmic abundance and its linear bias, measuring 103 ΩHibHi = 1.271_(-0.598)^(+1.080). This direct measurement marks a milestone in demonstrating the effectiveness of the Hi intensity mapping technique for future surveys with the SKA Observatory, of which MeerKAT is a precursor.

shortlist.title: Atomically resolved superconducting gap in (La,Pr) 3 Ni 2 O 7 films
shortlist.abstract: Ruddlesden-Popper bilayer nickelates provide an emerging platform for studying high-temperature superconductivity, yet the superconducting pairing symmetry remains under debate. Here, we use atomic-resolution scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy to investigate superconducting 1.5-unit-cell (La,Pr)3Ni2O7 films grown on SrLaAlO4. A cryogenic ultrahigh-vacuum (UHV) sample transfer preserves an ordered sqrt(2) * sqrt(2) surface and yields reproducible U-shaped spectra with two gap scales of ~14 and ~20 meV and extended flat zero-conductance bottoms. By contrast, samples exposed for a longer time in UHV without cooling during transfer show V-shaped spectra despite retaining the surface reconstruction and a transport superconducting transition onset above 40 K. Wide-energy-range spectra indicate that oxygen loss can mix density-wave-related spectral weight. Our measurements provide an atomic-scale observation of the intrinsic nodeless superconducting gap in bilayer nickelate ultrathin films.

shortlist.title: Benefiting from Culture Wars: Resource Mobilization in Polarized Issue Domains
shortlist.abstract: Organizations engaging with contested social issues may struggle to mobilize resources due to disapproval from hostile audiences. Yet, some may benefit from increased support from sympathetic audiences, leaving unclear when such support will outweigh opposition. We propose that variation in audience reactions depends partly on how contestation is structured. We theorize that ideological polarization—the extent to which opposing stances on an issue sort along ideological lines—may enhance resource mobilization in contested issue domains. As polarization increases, contested issues pit opposing identities against each other and heighten threats to sympathetic audiences’ worldviews. New ventures in more polarized domains may attract greater support as sympathetic audiences respond by investing in aligned ventures, a mechanism we term “compensatory investment.” This relationship strengthens under conditions that heighten identity threat: when issues are highly salient, making them central political battlegrounds, and when audiences on both sides rely on core moral foundations to evaluate the issue, so that disagreements are experienced as moral violations. Analyses of U.S.-based Kickstarter campaigns (2009–2020) support our predictions and provide evidence consistent with compensatory investment. Our study highlights polarization as a key source of issue heterogeneity, introduces the mechanism of compensatory investment, and specifies when polarization enhances resource mobilization.

shortlist.title: Controlling Rydberg atom-polariton interactions: from exceptional points to fast readout
shortlist.abstract: Rydberg atoms represent a platform underpinning many recent developments in quantum computation, simulation, sensing, and metrology. They further facilitate optical nonlinearity at the single-photon level when coupled to photons propagating in atomic clouds, which form collective atomic excitations called Rydberg polaritons, strongly interacting with each other. Here, we experimentally explore interactions between a Rydberg polariton in an atomic ensemble and a single, adjacent, Rydberg atom. We discover three different regimes of quantum dynamics corresponding to polariton blockade, coherent exchange, and probabilistic hopping, which are defined by their distinct transmission characteristics, with a transition through an exceptional point occurring between blockade and coherent exchange. We investigate the applications of such interactions for fast, non-destructive detection of Rydberg atoms and present proof-of-principle demonstrations for their potential application in nonlinear photonic networks.

shortlist.title: Dynamics of O(2) excitations in a non-reciprocal medium
shortlist.abstract: We investigate emergent dynamics due to non-reciprocity in the O(2) model. The lattice XY model, where non-reciprocity stems from vision cone like couplings, can be described by a continuum description in which non-reciprocity translates into a new term depending on the rotational of the orientation field. We argue that non-reciprocity is akin to activity and we highlight the connection between our hydrodynamic equation and the constant density Toner-Tu framework. The active force advects and reshapes patterns, a generic feature found in many non-reciprocal systems. We show how 1d excitations in the non-reciprocal O(2) model can be described by a generalized Burgers equation, derived from our continuum model. We then extend the results to 2d perturbations. As such, we establish the first principles of excitation trajectory control in a non-reciprocal O(2) medium. Concretely, we explain how tuning the degree of non-reciprocity and the orientation of the background medium impacts the time evolution of excitations. We also showcase how initially different excitations lead to very different dynamical behavior. Non-reciprocity also affects the stability of defect-free excitations with non-zero winding numbers and, unlike in its equilibrium O(2) counterpart, enables the system, above a certain threshold, to relax to its ground state.

shortlist.title: A two-phase model of galaxy formation: IV. Seeding and growing supermassive black holes in dark matter halos
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: We present a theoretical framework for seeding and growing supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in dark matter halos along their assembly histories. Seeds are bred out of Pop-III stars formed during the first collapse of pristine gas in mini-halos that have reached the H2-cooling limit, modulated by UV radiation from star formation and dynamical heating from fast halo assembly. Such breeding persists until the enrichment of the intergalactic medium (IGM) enables Pop-II stars to form. Post-seeding growth of black holes (BHs) is driven by distinct channels, starting with episodic super-Eddington accretion associated with nuclear bursts induced by global disturbances of galaxies, followed by sustained sub-Eddington accretion via capturing sub-clouds formed in self-gravitating gas clouds (SGCs) in halos of fast assembly, and ending with merger-dominated, quiescent growth. We implement the model in subhalo merger trees to build a coherent framework to follow SMBH-galaxy-halo co-evolution across the whole history and structural hierarchy. BH seeds are bred with a broad mass spectrum of M_(BH)= 10–105 M⊙ at z ≈ 20–30 in mini-halos with masses of 105–108 M⊙. Nuclear bursts provide the key condition for seeds to grow into SMBHs. The M_(BH)-M* relation is a multi-piece, redshift-dependent function shaped by the interplay among different growth channels. Our model predictions are broadly consistent with existing observations; in particular, a population of BHs reminiscent of ‘little red dots’ (LRDs) discovered by JWST naturally results from the seeding and growing processes. Potential future tests of the model are discussed.

shortlist.title: How to raise a supermassive black hole: interpreting early JWST AGN with the AESOPICA simulations
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: The active galactic nuclei (AGN) uncovered by JWST in the early Universe are highly abundant and seemingly overmassive with respect to local scaling relations, challenging standard models of black hole formation and growth. Yet it remains unclear whether they trace an efficient early growth channel, represent the observable tail of a broader population, or reflect systematic uncertainties in mass estimates. We introduce the aesopica project, a suite of twelve mid-volume (L = 60 cMpc) cosmological simulations based on the fable galaxy formation model, varying the black hole seed mass across the theoretical formation channels (Mseed = 102–105 M⊙), the accretion efficiency, including super-Eddington bursts, and the supernova feedback strength. We forward-model observational selection with balmersopica, a mock JWST broad-line survey pipeline that assesses the detectability of each simulated AGN for a given grating and exposure time. We find that the bulk of the JWST AGN population can be assembled from any seed mass provided the accretion efficiency is high, although light seeds require the most favourable accretion conditions explored. Applying broad-line selection naturally recovers the apparently overmassive population, with the detected AGN lying furthest above the intrinsic MBH–Mstellar relation for inefficient accretion models. The selected AGN lie on the local, weakly evolving MBH–σstellar relation, supporting a scenario where black holes assemble before the stellar component is fully established. Since efficient accretion rapidly erases the imprint of the initial seed mass, the low-mass end of the black hole mass function and host gas-phase metallicities offer the most promising discriminants between seeding channels.

shortlist.title: Saturation genome editing of BRCA1 across cell types improves interpretation of variant pathogenicity
shortlist.abstract: Germline pathogenic BRCA1 variants predispose women to breast and ovarian cancer. Despite accumulation of functional evidence, over half of reported single-nucleotide variants in BRCA1 lack a definitive clinical interpretation. Furthermore, the consistency of variant effects across cell types remains largely unexplored. Here we performed saturation genome editing (SGE) of BRCA1 in HAP1 cells to score 4,113 previously unassayed variants. Additionally, we developed an SGE assay in human mammary epithelial cells (HMECs), allowing comparison of effects across cell lines, drug treatments and genetic backgrounds. We identified 538 variants impacting gene function through distinct mechanisms. HAP1 function scores discriminate between known pathogenic and benign variants with near-perfect accuracy. Intriguingly, however, nearly half of HAP1 loss-of-function variants scored neutrally in HMECs. We show that discordantly scored variants are hypomorphic and confer intermediate cancer risk. Overall, this work demonstrates how performing SGE across cell models improves the functional interpretation of rare variants.

shortlist.title: In situ profiling of plasma cell clonality with image-based single-cell transcriptomics
shortlist.abstract: Image-based single-cell transcriptomics can identify diverse cell types in intact tissues. However, in adaptive immunity, V(D)J recombination generates unique immune receptors in cells of the same type, leading to important functional variation that is not yet defined by these methods. Here we introduce B cell receptor multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (BCR-MERFISH), which measures plasma cell clonality based on V gene usage in combination with transcriptome profiling. We demonstrate that BCR-MERFISH accurately identifies V gene usage in cell culture and in mice with restricted or native plasma cell diversity. We then use BCR-MERFISH to elucidate the microbiota-dependent changes in plasma cell abundance, clonal diversity, and public clonotype usage in the mouse gut and the non-uniform distribution of plasma cell clones along the mouse ileum. Given that tissue context is an essential modulator of plasma cell dynamics, we anticipate that BCR-MERFISH may offer new insights into a wide range of immunological questions.

shortlist.title: Optimal Policy Rules in HANK
shortlist.abstract: We characterize optimal policy rules in a business-cycle model with nominal rigidities and heterogeneous households. The policymaker has access to two instruments: the short-term nominal rate, and lump-sum transfer payments. A policymaker with a traditional dual mandate that targets aggregates uses the same policy rule as is optimal in the textbook New Keynesian model. We then consider a policymaker with a distributional objective. The optimal policy rule now contains an additional term, reflecting the effects of the policymaker’s instruments on consumption inequality. Since, in our model, monetary policy only has very limited distributional effects, this additional term does not materially change optimal monetary policy. Fiscal stimulus payments, on the other hand, have strongly progressive effects and are thus well-suited to cushion the distributional effects of cyclical fluctuations.

shortlist.title: The Influence of Police Unions in Local Elections: Evidence from U.S. Cities’ Spending and Performance
shortlist.abstract: Despite growing attention to local policies governing public safety issues, and mounting reports of police union spending to local candidates, the role of police unions in local politics remains understudied. We address this gap by assembling a novel, large-scale dataset on campaign finance in U.S. mayoral elections, covering 2,303 races across 1,073 cities from 2001 to 2019. We document that police unions frequently donate to mayoral candidates—especially in mid-sized and large cities—targeting likely winners and incumbents, and without displaying clear partisan bias. Using a within-city design that accounts for heterogeneous treatment effects in the presence of staggered treatment timing, we find that the election of a police-union-backed mayor leads to an expansion in police department size. However, we do not find improvements in police performance in these cities, suggesting that unions’ political involvement, while providing additional resources, might also be associated with reduced incentives for effort.

shortlist.title: Fast, high-fidelity erasure detection of dual-rail qubits with symmetrically coupled readout
shortlist.abstract: Erasure qubits are a promising platform for implementing hardware-efficient quantum error correction. Realizing the error-correction advantages of this encoding requires frequent mid-circuit erasure checks that are fast, high-fidelity, and scalable. Here, we realize erasure detection with a hardware-efficient circuit consisting of a single readout resonator dispersively and symmetrically coupled to both transmons of a dual-rail qubit. We use this circuit to demonstrate single-shot erasure detection in 384 ns with minimal impact on the dual-rail logical manifold, achieving a residual error per check of 6.0(2) × 10⁻⁴, with only 8(3) × 10⁻⁵ induced dephasing per check, and an erasure error per check of 2.54(1)× 10⁻². The high degree of matched dispersive readout coupling (χ-matching) within the dual-rail qubit code space also allows us to realize a new modality: time-continuous erasure detection performed in parallel with single-qubit gates. Here we achieve a median 7.2 × 10⁻⁵ error per gate with < 1 × 10⁻⁵ error induced by erasure detection. This demonstrates a reduction in erasure detection overhead as well as a crucial ingredient for soft information quantum error correction. Together, these results establish symmetrically coupled dispersive readout as a fast, hardware-efficient, and scalable component for erasure-based quantum error correction using transmon dual-rail qubits.

shortlist.title: Daddy’s Girl: Daughters, Managerial Decisions, and Gender Inequality
shortlist.abstract: Using Danish registry data, we study how managers’ gender attitudes shape gender inequality in the workplace by exploiting the birth of a daughter—as opposed to a son—as a plausibly exogenous shock to male managers’ gender attitudes. Comparing within-firm changes in women’s labour outcomes depending on the gender of the manager’s newborn child, we find that women’s relative earnings and employment increase by 4.4% and 2.9%, respectively, following the birth of the manager’s first daughter. These effects are driven by an increase in managers’ propensity to substitute male hires with female hires that have comparable education, hours worked, and earnings. Consistent with this substitution channel, we do not detect any significant effect on firm performance. Because these effects emerge rapidly and persist over time, we can rule out the need for prolonged exposure to gender issues or for personal incentives tied to improving conditions for their own daughters as prerequisites for managers to promote gender equality within their firms.

shortlist.title: Limitations of de novo peptide sequencing in resolving sequence ambiguity
shortlist.abstract: De novo peptide sequencing enables peptide identification from fragmentation spectra without relying on sequence databases. However, incomplete spectra create ambiguity, making unambiguous identification challenging. Recent deep learning advances have produced numerous de novo models that predict sequences and refine peptide-spectrum matches under such conditions. Yet, their relative strengths, weaknesses and ability to handle spectrum ambiguity remain unclear. Here we benchmark eight state-of-the-art models on three publicly available proteomics datasets, comparing performance using established metrics and quantifying inter-model agreement. We assess post-processing approaches, including iterative refinement, rescoring and reranking, for their ability to improve identification accuracy, and perform an error analysis to identify common mispredictions and their causes. Model performance varied, with considerable overlap of correct identifications. Post-processing yielded no or only modest improvements. Most sequencing errors were model-independent and driven by limited fragment ion coverage, a limitation also observed in database searches with large search spaces.

fundamentals.title: Operator structure of power corrections and anomalous scaling in energy correlators
fundamentals.abstract: Energy correlators offer a clean probe of quantum chromodynamics, serving as an ideal laboratory to rigorously investigate non-perturbative power corrections. The recent discovery that linear corrections exhibit a universal anomalous scaling points to a deep, underlying theoretical structure. We uncover the quantum field-theoretic origin of this phenomenon in the energy-energy correlator using light-ray operators. Through an explicit loop calculation, we derive the one-loop anomalous dimension, revealing that the dijet operator must be combined with a specific triple-jet component. This provides a first-principles framework that connects operator theory with high-precision collider phenomenology.

fundamentals.title: Unified theory of quartz tuning fork resonators
fundamentals.abstract: Quartz tuning forks, functioning as electrically driven piezoelectric resonators, have long served as exceptionally stable and widely adopted timing references in diverse domains of research and industry. Yet, experimentally measured electrical resonance spectra often exhibit resonance evolutions that remain unexplained within existing theoretical descriptions. Here we develop a unified continuum electromechanical modal framework that integrates piezoelectric electrodynamics, variational structural dynamics, and symmetry-selected electromechanical observability. Our theory shows quantitative agreement with experimental results, demonstrating that electrical observability emerges not from the underlying mechanical eigenmodes alone. The resulting framework unifies conventional coupled-oscillator, equivalent-circuit, and continuum descriptions within a single first-principles theory and provides a rigorous basis for precision electromechanical characterization.

fundamentals.title: Phase transition in a dryland shrub–grass ecosystem: Emergence through local trade-offs
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Ecosystems are complex adaptive systems in which local interactions among individuals shape macroscopic phenomena such as pattern formation, multistability, and critical transitions. However, how such bottom-up interactions govern emergent behaviors and system-level complexity remains a central challenge in ecology. Phase transition theory, a classic paradigm in physics, links local interaction rules to emergent changes in macroscopic system states, offering a formal language for understanding cross-scale dynamics. Here we unite this theory with empirical evidence from dryland shrub-grass ecosystems and show that these systems exhibit three hallmarks of phase transitions. First, abrupt shifts separate different phases of deserts, shrublands, and grasslands. Second, shrublands and grasslands self-organize into Turing-like phase patterns, contrasting with homogeneous deserts. Third, special phenomena emerge near-transition threshold, including patch enlargement and abrupt decline at desert-vegetation interface, and fairy circles within the shrub-grass transition zone. Using a cellular automaton model built on a fundamental trade-off between extensive and intensive resource foraging strategies (EI trade-off), we show how kernels encoding local trade-offs integrate these seemingly disparate phenomena within a unified phase transition framework. Moreover, this EI trade-off was empirically validated through analyses of plant functional traits and spatial patterns of plant patches. These findings illustrate that dryland ecosystem dynamics reflect universal self-organization principles. Our work establishes phase-transition theory as a powerful framework for understanding, predicting, and managing complexity in dryland ecosystems, which advances the integration of complexity…

fundamentals.title: Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance
fundamentals.abstract: The evolution of quantum states can be described by quantum channels. The task of estimating an unknown quantum channel, known as process tomography, is a central problem in quantum information theory. A long-standing open question is how many uses of an unknown channel are required to learn it to a precision quantified by the standard metric for distinguishing quantum processes, known as the diamond distance. Here we address this by establishing the query complexity of channel tomography with optimal dependence on the dimensions of the input and output spaces and the channel’s Kraus rank at any fixed constant accuracy in diamond distance. We design an algorithm that establishes an upper bound and prove a matching lower bound for learning a channel to the given accuracy. Our algorithm follows the strategy of performing optimal tomography on the Choi-state representation of the process, and we show that channel tomography can be reduced to the well-studied problem of pure-state tomography. As channels subsume states, unitaries and measurements as special cases, our protocol provides a unified framework for tomography of these tasks.

fig.label: Figure 1
fig.caption: Protocol for learning quantum channels. Parallel invocations of the unknown channel Λ , applied to halves of maximally entangled states |Ω⟩ , prepare copies of its normalised Choi state Φ_c=J(Λ) . A purification channel then maps these Choi-state copies to copies of a random purification |Φ_c⟩ , which are learned using a sample-optimal pure-state tomography scheme. Finally, a classical post-processing step, formulated as a semidefinite program projecting onto the set of CPTP maps, returns a channel estimate Λ̂ satisfying ‖Λ̂-Λ‖_◇≤ε with high probability.

fundamentals.title: Sound propagation in striped supersolid gases at zero temperature
fundamentals.abstract: The role of dimensionality in the identification of sound modes in many-body systems characterized by the spontaneous breaking of translational symmetry is a topic of high interdisciplinary interest in both classical and quantum systems. The emergence of stripes in superfluids is a particularly interesting example where the dimensionality of the system differs from the one of the crystal phase. Here we present a unified hydrodynamic approach for the sound propagation in the stripe phase realized in ultracold dipolar and spin-orbit-coupled Bose gases at zero temperature. Despite the deep difference of the two platforms at a microscopic level, a similar hydrodynamic description can be formulated at a macroscopic level. The main difference between the two platforms is the lack of Galilean invariance in the spin-orbit case, resulting in a different identification of the normal (non-superfluid) component of the density. In both cases the spectrum comprises two sounds, reflecting the spontaneous breaking of the U(1) and translational symmetries. Both sounds exhibit an anisotropic behavior. A comparison with the first and second sounds of the smectic-A liquid crystal is also presented.

fundamentals.title: Passage of particles through matter and the effective straggling-function: High-fidelity accelerated simulation via Physics-Informed Machine Learning
fundamentals.abstract: High-fidelity simulation of particle-matter interactions provides the essential theoretical reference for diverse physics disciplines, yet generating synthetic datasets at the scale of current and future experiments has become prohibitive. Here, we introduce PHIN-GAN, a novel physics-informed generative adversarial network designed to address this challenge. We derive a set of analytical probability density functions, that effectively describe the ``straggling function'' identified with Landau. For the first time, this enables their continuous evaluation across the entire phase-space. These analytical forms are leveraged to enforce a parametric distribution-level learning objective. Rooted in first principles, PHIN-GAN offers a generalizable, interpretable and scalable proof-of-concept approach for a lossless generative model that maintains the high fidelity of the standard-bearer for simulating such interactions, namely GEANT4, at a fraction of the computational cost.

fundamentals.title: The Huang–Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
fundamentals.abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin 1/2 1 / 2 fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.

fundamentals.title: Similarity Solutions of Shock Formation for First-Order Strictly Hyperbolic Systems
fundamentals.abstract: Shocks due to hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) appear throughout mathematics and science. The canonical example is shock formation in the inviscid Burgers equation [Formula: see text]. Previous studies have shown that when shocks form for the inviscid Burgers equation, for positions and times close to the shock singularity, the dynamics are locally self-similar and universal, i.e., dynamics are equivalent regardless of the initial conditions. In this paper, we show that, in fact, shock formation is self-similar and universal for general first-order strictly hyperbolic PDEs in one spatial dimension, and the self-similarity is like that of the inviscid Burgers equation. An analytical formula is derived for the self-similar universal solution. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SIREV and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.34770/6vgh-br25 and in the supplementary materials ( M180373_SM.zip [25.7MB]). fundamentals.title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
fundamentals.abstract: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

fundamentals.title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
fundamentals.abstract: The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. Furthermore, recognizing the strong synergies between inverse methods and machine learning offers the opportunity to establish a coherent framework applicable to both fields. Differentiating functions based on the numerical solution of differential equations is nontrivial. Numerous methods based on a wide variety of paradigms have been proposed in the literature, each with pros and cons specific to the type of problem investigated. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of existing techniques to compute derivatives of numerical solutions of differential equations. We first discuss the importance of gradients of solutions of differential equations in a variety of scientific domains. Second, we lay out and compare the mathematical foundations of the various approaches. Third, we cover computational considerations and explore the solutions available in modern scientific software. Last but not least, we provide best practices and recommendations for practitioners. We hope that this work accelerates the fusion of scientific models and data and fosters a modern approach to scientific modeling.

fundamentals.title: Reconciling Discrete-Time Mixed Policies and Continuous-Time Relaxed Controls in Reinforcement Learning and Stochastic Control
fundamentals.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is currently one of the most prominent methods for optimizing dynamical systems, with breakthrough results across various fields. The framework is based on the concept of a Markov decision process (MDP), leading to a discrete-time optimal control problem. In the RL literature, such problems are typically formulated and solved using mixed policies, from which random actions are sampled at each time step. Recently, part of the optimal control community has begun investigating continuous-time versions of RL algorithms, replacing MDPs with continuous-time stochastic processes governed by relaxed controls and asserting a full analogy between the two formulations. In this work, we examine the limitations of this analogy and rigorously establish a connection between the two problems in the case where only the drift term of the continuous-time model is controlled. We prove strong convergence of the RL implementation of mixed strategies as the time discretization mesh tends to zero. We also discuss the technical challenges posed by the possible presence of control in the diffusion component of the state.
