fundamentals.title: Effective gaps between singular values of non-stationary matrix products subject to non-degenerate noise
fundamentals.abstract: We study the singular values and Lyapunov exponents of non-stationary random matrix products subject to small, absolutely continuous, additive noise. Consider a fixed sequence of matrices of bounded norm. Independently perturb the matrices by additive noise distributed according to Lebesgue measure on matrices with norm less than ε ϵ . Then the gaps between the logarithms of the singular values of the random product of n n of these matrices are all of order at least ε ²n ϵ 2 n , both in expectation; and almost surely for large n n . To prove this, we develop recent work of Gorodetski and Kleptsyn [26]. That paper gives a very flexible method, based on relative entropy, for showing that a non-stationary product of matrices in SL(d,R) SL ( d , R ) has a strictly positive Lyapunov exponent. We extend their work in two ways, firstly by making the estimates quantitative in the context of absolutely continuous distributions, giving the universal estimates described above; and secondly by developing a fibered version of their methods, working on flag bundles instead of the projective space to estimate gaps between arbitrary consecutive exponents. Our methods retain much of the flexibility of those of Gorodetski and Kleptsyn, and we hope that they will find application in other related problems.

fundamentals.title: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? If so, how does the low dimensionality enable predictions with limited information? Here, we report an emergent simplicity that the temporal dynamics of observable microbial populations can be captured by low-dimensional representations. Using variational autoencoders, we define a critical latent dimension ( E c ) that operationally quantifies the smallest latent dimension required for high-fidelity reconstruction of observable microbial dynamics under a specified criterion. Despite the complexity of unobserved background dynamics, we find E c to be drastically lower than the community’s apparent degrees of freedom. E c scales linearly with the number of observables, providing an empirical principle for determining representation complexity. This principle holds across simulations of pairwise interacting communities, consumer–resource dynamics, spatially distributed microbial patches, and plasmid transfer, experiments with engineered and environment-derived communities, and human microbiomes. Our findings establish a scaling law for microbial community dynamics and demonstrate that low-dimensional representations of observable dynamics retain information useful for selected prediction tasks without direct measurement of the complete community.

fundamentals.title: Foiling Black Hole Foils: Revealing Horizon Alternatives with Baryonic Atmospheres
fundamentals.abstract: Event horizons are a defining feature of black holes. Consequently, there have been many efforts to probe their existence in astrophysical black hole candidates, spanning 10 orders of magnitude in mass. Nevertheless, horizons remain an obstacle to unifying general relativity and quantum mechanics, most sharply presented by the information paradox. This has motivated a proliferation of horizonless alternatives (black hole foils) that avoid event horizons and are therefore presumably benign. We explore the fate of accreting material in the context of spherically symmetric horizonless compact objects in the steady state regime. We find that for typical accreting astronomical targets, foils can develop an optically thick, convectively stable baryonic atmosphere, immediately implying the creation of an emitting photosphere at modest redshift even when the surface redshift is extreme. The emergent photosphere luminosity is driven toward the accretion powered equilibrium value and is only weakly sensitive to the foil redshift. Moreover, local gas–surface interaction provides a microphysical lower bound on the effective base temperature, insulating the atmosphere from arbitrarily cold foils. The unknown properties of the foil enter only through local boundary conditions controlling baryon processing and thermal coupling at the surface, making the solutions broadly applicable to horizonless alternatives that do not invoke significant additional nonlocal interactions. Thus, under minimal assumptions (GR exterior and local surface interactions), spherically symmetric horizonless foils in accreting systems are generically observationally exposed: the absence of a thermal photosphere directly constrains or rules out broad classes of such models.

fundamentals.title: Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
fundamentals.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

fundamentals.title: Bright Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn: A Cloud-Scale Star Formation Model Unifying Variable SFE, IMFs, and Stochasticity
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: To investigate the origins of the high abundance of UV-bright galaxies at z > 10, we present a new semi-analytic model that bridges the gap between small-scale star formation physics and large-scale galaxy evolution by explicitly tracking discrete star-forming clouds within smoothly evolving dark matter potentials. Unlike conventional semi-analytic models, our approach naturally captures the stochasticity of star formation, allowing us to isolate how cloud properties, star formation efficiencies (SFEs), and stellar initial mass functions (IMFs) shape the star-formation burstiness of early galaxies. Clouds are drawn sequentially from a cloud mass distribution, assigned an SFE and IMF depending on cloud mass, metallicity, and redshift, and evolve under the influence of short-timescale stellar feedback. We identify three distinct star formation regimes arising from the interplay between cloud masses, densities, and feedback timescales: a stochastic, feedback-limited regime in low-mass halos with long quiescent phases; a bursty regime regulated by the cloud mass distribution; and a smooth, continuous regime in massive halos. Our fiducial model adopts a dynamic IMF, an SFE linked to cloud properties and the IMF, and massive, moderately dense clouds. Varying assumptions reveals that top-heavy IMFs and enhanced SFEs in massive clouds amplify burstiness, while altering the upper cloud mass or density normalisation is secondary. Among model ingredients, the IMF most strongly impacts the UV luminosity function (LF), while switching to a constant SFE boosts the faint end, and reducing the maximum cloud mass decreases the bright end. These results demonstrate that cloud-scale physics critically shape early galaxy UV luminosity distributions.

fundamentals.title: The commutativity problem for effective varieties of formal series, and applications
fundamentals.abstract: A formal series in noncommuting variables Σ over the rationals is a mapping Σ * → Q from the free monoid generated by Σ to the rationals. We say that it is commutative if the output does not depend on the order of the symbols in the input. The commutativity problem for a class of series takes as input a (finite presentation of) a series from the class and amounts to establishing whether it is commutative. This is a very natural, albeit nontrivial problem, which has not been considered before from an algorithmic perspective. We show that commutativity is decidable for all classes of series that constitute a so-called effective prevariety , a notion generalising Reutenauer’s varieties of formal series. For example, the class of rational series , introduced by Schützenberger in the 1960’s, is well-known to be an effective (pre)variety, and thus commutativity is decidable for it. In order to showcase the applicability of our result, we consider classes of formal series generalising the rational ones. We consider polynomial automata , shuffle automata , and infiltration automata , and we show that each of these models recognises an effective prevariety of formal series. Consequently, their commutativity problem is decidable, which is a novel result. We find it remarkable that commutativity can be decided in a uniform way for such disparate computation models. Finally, we present applications of commutativity outside the theory of formal series. We show that we can decide solvability in sequences and in power series for restricted classes of algebraic difference and differential equations, for which such problems are undecidable in full generality. Thanks to this, we can prove that the syntaxes of multivariate polynomial recursive sequences and of constructible…

fundamentals.title: Substitutional Quantification and Arithmetical Truth
fundamentals.abstract: In the mid‐20th century, there was a debate about whether the quantifiers in first‐order logic should be understood objectually or substitutionally. This debate typically focused on ontology and assumed that we could use only one of these two types of quantification. After Kripke and others influentially argued that the two kinds of quantification were logically equivalent, defenses of substitutional quantification were rare. Following Gottlieb and Field, I argue that Kripke was wrong and that substitutional consequence is language‐bound and non‐compact. While of no help with ontology, I also argue that so‐understood, substitutional quantification can be applied to help explain our grasp of a determinate notion of arithmetical truth. To argue for this, I give an account of the metasemantics of the substitutional quantifiers and prove that adding a single, very natural, mixed axiom to weak theories of arithmetic results in a categorical theory. This approach promises to explain arithmetical truth on a less controversial basis than appeals to either second‐order logic or the omega rule, thus making progress on the project of explaining our grasp of arithmetic in a naturalistically acceptable fashion.

fundamentals.title: Tidal Deformation and Strain Accumulation of Solid Compact Stars
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The tidal deformability of compact stars encodes the equation of state of dense matter, and gravitational-wave observations such as GW170817 have begun to constrain it under the assumption of a fluid interior. Yet whether the interior of pulsar-like compact stars is fluid or solid remains largely untested, despite the distinct tidal responses the two states predict. In this work, based on the strangeon-star model, we develop a framework for modeling tidal deformation in solid compact stars. Adopting a shear modulus of μ = 1034 erg cm−3, we find a relative difference of approximately 30 % in tidal deformability between solid and fluid strangeon stars of 1.4 M⊙, corresponding to a ~10 % deviation from the universal I–Love relation. We further model the accumulation of internal strain during binary inspiral and find that it peaks near the stellar center. When the gravitational-wave frequency reaches several hundred Hz, the strain in a large fraction of the stellar volume exceeds the adopted threshold σ = 10−3, and the elastic energy stored in the threshold-exceeding region reaches ~1046 erg at these frequencies. A solid-to-fluid transition would alter the tidal response and could imprint on the waveform and phase of the emitted gravitational radiation. Combined with the precursor electromagnetic emission, these gravitational-wave signatures offer a multi-messenger avenue to test the solid nature of pulsar-like compact stars.

fundamentals.title: Improving Lives and Avoiding Harm
fundamentals.abstract: The Asymmetry in population ethics holds that creating a miserable person is morally impermissible, while not creating a happy person is morally permissible, all else being equal. Harm‐avoidance theories explain the Asymmetry by claiming that, in certain contexts, only actions resulting in harm are impermissible. Two problems threaten these theories: (i) The Problem of Improvable Life Avoidance—requiring agents to avoid creating improvable good lives—and (ii) requiring dominated options. Sophisticated harm‐avoidance theories avoid both problems. However, we show that any harm‐avoidance theory entails either (1) a worse form of The Problem of Improvable Life Avoidance, (2) a troubling form of sadism, (3) an implausibly extreme priority for avoiding a small harm for one person over greater harms for many people, or (4) spurious prohibition dilemmas. Furthermore, we argue that any reasonable theory of the Asymmetry entails at least one of (1)–(4).

fundamentals.title: A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows τα∝B−2. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-B pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with 1012 G, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.

fundamentals.title: The Wild West of Nomenclature, Definitions, and Methodologies in Rodent Sleep Scoring
fundamentals.abstract: Rodent models are essential for investigating the mechanisms and regulation of sleep, yet the field lacks a unified framework for sleep-scoring terminology, definitions, and reporting. Laboratories vary in recording modalities, temporal resolution, staging criteria, and analytical approaches, reflecting both historical practices and the diverse experimental questions addressed using rodent models. Ongoing efforts to harmonize and standardize rodent sleep methodologies are therefore important for improving rigor, reproducibility, and cross-study comparison. However, methodological harmonization also requires a shared vocabulary and clear operational definitions to understand how scoring and analytical approaches are implemented and how methodological choices influence reported outcomes. In this Perspective, we examine variability surrounding fundamental constructs in rodent sleep analysis, including epochs, bouts, segments, fragmentation, and consolidation. We illustrate how choices such as epoch duration and bout initiation, continuation, and termination criteria can alter sleep-stage assignment, bout number and duration, transition frequency, and ultimately the apparent fragmentation or consolidation of sleep. We further distinguish epochs, defined as temporal units receiving vigilance-state assignments, from segments used for signal processing, feature extraction, or data aggregation, and emphasize the importance of defining the specific metrics used to characterize fragmentation and consolidation. Complementing broader efforts to harmonize rodent sleep methodologies, we propose consistent terminology, explicit operational definitions, and minimum reporting practices that make methodological and analytical decisions transparent across recording and scoring…

fundamentals.title: Invariance, Stability, and Diversity: A Unified Framework for Multimodal Domain Generalization
fundamentals.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
fundamentals.abstract: Multimodal Domain Generalization (MMDG) aims to learn models that generalize to unseen domains under unpredictable, modality-dependent distribution shifts. Despite recent progress, existing methods often rely on heuristic fusion strategies and lack a unified theoretical perspective, limiting their robustness under domain shifts. In this paper, we identify three fundamental challenges in MMDG: (I) insufficient cross-domain invariance across individual modalities and cross-modal interaction subspaces; (II) instability induced by asynchronous modality degradation, through which unreliable modalities impair joint representations; and (III) limited representation diversity, which exacerbates source-target support mismatch. To characterize these challenges, we derive a generalization error bound for a stability-weighted ensemble of modality-wise hypotheses, revealing three corresponding factors: Invariance (Source-Source Divergence), Stability (Stability-Weighted Error), and Diversity (Target-Convex Hull Divergence). Guided by this analysis, we develop a unified nonlinear fusion framework comprising Multi-Granularity Adversarial Alignment to promote invariance across modality-specific, interaction, and fusion spaces, Stability-Aware Adaptive Learning to prioritize reliable modalities during source training and mitigate asynchronous degradation, and Manifold Expansion to increase normalized source-feature dispersion as a source-side regularizer. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks show that our framework achieves the best overall average rank across 43 transfer tasks on seven datasets spanning four task families and eight diverse modalities.

fundamentals.title: On the Orbital Evolution of Giant-planet Pair Embedded in a Gaseous Disk. III. Simultaneous Gas Accretion and the Final Mass Ratio
fundamentals.abstract: Recent exoplanet surveys reveal a systematic trend in the mass ratios of giant-planet pairs (>30 M ⊕ ). Although the M outer / M inner is broadly centered near unity, it exhibits a dependence on orbital separation. Compact pairs tend to have comparable masses, whereas widely separated pairs show outer-heavy configurations. To investigate the origin of this trend, we perform 2D hydrodynamic simulations that couple gas accretion and orbital migration of two giant planet embryos with initial masses of 15−30 M ⊕ . We explore the effects of disk viscosity, surface density slope, and initial mass ratio on the coupled evolution of planetary growth and migration. We find that convergent migration drives the planets to open a common gap, restructuring the gas flow. This configuration induces asymmetric accretion, in which the inner planet becomes starved as gap clearing suppresses its gas supply, while the outer planet continues to accrete from the high-density region at the outer gap edge. Consequently, the system naturally evolves toward mass-ratio convergence, and in many cases produces an inversion of the initial core-mass hierarchy. We further show that migration outcomes are highly sensitive to initial conditions. Systems with initially more massive inner cores tend to diverge, whereas steeper surface density profiles and more massive outer cores favor convergent migration and subsequent resonance capture. Overall, our results identify common-gap-driven asymmetric accretion as a unified mechanism linking orbital architecture, resonant capture, and the observed mass-ratio demographics of giant planet pairs.

fundamentals.title: A Unified Reactivity Scale Predicts Nonenzymatic Phosphoryl Transfer and Nucleophilic Catalysis in Water
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. Together,…

food.title: Impact of arsenic exposure on the gut-microbiota-liver axis in poultry
food.abstract: Arsenic (As), a priority hazardous substance widely distributed in nature, endangers poultry health and food safety. The gut‑microbiota‑liver axis forms a bidirectional regulatory network, with the intestine acting as the main absorption site and the liver as the key metabolic‑detoxification organ for As. This review summarizes arsenic‑induced toxic injuries to this axis in poultry. In the intestine, As impairs mucosal barrier function, triggers epithelial cell death via NF‑κB‑NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and causes leaky‑gut syndrome. It also disturbs gut microbiota homeostasis, lowering beneficial butyrate‑producing bacteria and impairing short‑chain‑fatty‑acid synthesis. In the liver, As disrupts energy metabolism, provokes severe oxidative stress, and triggers multiple forms of programmed cell death, including ferroptosis and PANoptosis. Gut-derived lipopolysaccharide translocates to the liver via the portal circulation, amplifying hepatic inflammation, which in turn causes altered bile acid metabolism and reduced short-chain fatty acid production, thereby triggering gut microbiota dysbiosis and forming a self-reinforcing vicious cycle. Potential interventions including probiotics, polysaccharides, selenium and vitamin E are discussed to counteract arsenic toxicity. This work provides theoretical support for arsenic risk control in poultry farming.

food.title: Prevalence and levels of mycotoxins in poultry feed and ingredients: a global systematic review and meta-analysis
food.abstract: Mycotoxins are a global concern due to their widespread occurrence throughout the food chain and their potential risks to human and animal health. This study investigated the global prevalence and concentrations of mycotoxins in poultry feed and its components, assessing their potential health implication. Following the PRISMA methodology, 78 articles were included, with data processed (outlier removal) and analysed using STATA®. Globally, fumonisins B1 (FB1) and B2 (FB2) were the most prevalent (70% and 68%), with concentrations of 1,159 µg kg –1 and 164 µg kg –1 , respectively. The prevalence of aflatoxins (AFs), zearalenone (ZEN), deoxynivalenol (DON), ochratoxins (OTs), T-2/HT-2 toxins, emerging (overall pooled value of fusaric acid (FUS), enniatins (ENNs), apicidin (API), alternariol (AOH), nivalenol (NIV), beauvericin (BEA), patulin (PAT), moniliformin (MON), diacetoxyscirpenol (DAS), ergot alkaloids (EA), kojic acid (KA), tenuazonic acid (TeA), scirpentriol (SCIRP), cyclopiazonic acid (CPA), citrinin (CIT), fusarenon-X (FUS-X), T-2 triol/tetraol, and sterigmatocystin (STG)), and masked/modified mycotoxins (overall pooled value of deoxynivalenol-3-glucoside (D3G), 3-acetyl-deoxynivalenol (3-Ac-DON), and 15-acetyl-deoxynivalenol (15-Ac-DON)) appeared as 64%, 59%, 46%, 41%, 45%, 53% and 37%, with corresponding concentrations of 25.2, 204, 522, 36.6, 154, 15.8 and 35.0 µg kg –1 , respectively. Cotton, barley, sunflower, and maize meals showed high concentrations of multiple mycotoxins ( viz ., ZEN, FBs, and DON). Except for the AFs, all concentrations were below the Maximum Limits (MLs)/Guidance Values (GVs) established by the European Commission (EC 2002; EC 2006). food.title: Genetic dissection of carcass composition and fat deposition traits in a Pekin duck × Liancheng White duck F₂ population using univariate and cross-trait GWAS
food.abstract: Single-trait and multi-trait genome-wide association studies (C-GWAS) were performed on 18 carcass- and growth-related traits in a Pekin duck × Liancheng White duck F₂ population (n = 242; slaughtered at 70 d) using 12.8 million SNPs. Single-trait GWAS identified major-effect loci for carcass weight and half-eviscerated weight on chromosome 2 (104.68 Mb), for leg muscle weight on chromosome 2 (57.91 Mb), and for abdominal fat weight and skin fat thickness on chromosome 3 (88.46 Mb), revealing heterogeneous genetic architectures ranging from major-effect variants to polygenic backgrounds; the broad signal intervals were consistent with long-range LD in the F₂ population. Multi-trait C-GWAS substantially improved detection power, identifying 79022 genome-wide significant SNPs (P < 5×10⁻⁸), of which 69.9% were located within gene regions-markedly higher than the genomic background (∼45%). Functional enrichment of the 7,889 annotated candidate genes highlighted cell adhesion, actin cytoskeleton organization, and focal adhesion as core biological themes, with the IgSF-CAM signaling pathway (apla04517, Padjust = 2.9×10⁻¹²) as the most significantly enriched KEGG pathway-a signal not detected in single-trait analyses. Tissue-specific eQTL colocalization identified liver (33471 pairs) and muscle (29426 pairs) as the primary effector tissues, with MLH3 showing pleiotropic signals across multiple tissues, NGEF exhibiting muscle-specific enrichment, and PINK1 dominant in liver. Integrating SNP annotation, functional enrichment, and eQTL colocalization, six high-confidence candidate genes (MLH3, NGEF, PINK1, PRDM16, PTK2, and CADM2) were prioritized. food.title: Protocatechuic acid attenuates lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammatory responses in chicken macrophages by modulating the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway
food.abstract: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This study aimed to investigate the effects of PCA on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory responses in HD11 cells and its potential mechanisms of action. The regulatory effects of PCA on LPS-induced inflammatory responses were systematically evaluated by detecting nitric oxide (NO), reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammation-related factors, and protein expression, combined with transcriptomic sequencing analysis. The results showed that LPS stimulation significantly increased the production of NO and ROS in HD11 cells and upregulated the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-8 (IL-8). In contrast, PCA treatment reduced NO and ROS levels, downregulated the expression of IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-8, and increased interleukin-10 (IL-10) expression. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that PCA modulated genes and signaling pathways associated with innate immunity and inflammatory signal transduction, including the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway. Western blot analysis further demonstrated that PCA significantly reduced LPS-induced protein expression of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88), as well as the expression of the downstream inflammatory effector proteins inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2). Collectively, PCA effectively alleviated LPS-induced inflammatory responses and oxidative stress in HD11 cells, and its anti-inflammatory effects may involve the modulation of the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway and inhibition of inflammatory effector protein expression. food.title: Novel electron transport powers archaeal methane metabolism across varied substrates and environments
food.abstract: Methanogens are responsible for producing approximately one billion metric tons of methane each year within Earth’s anaerobic environments as a byproduct of their energy metabolism. They play a vital role in the global carbon cycle. There are three main pathways for methanogenesis: hydrogenotrophic, which uses H 2 and CO 2 to produce methane; methylotrophic, which utilizes methylated compounds like methanol and amines; and aceticlastic, which converts acetate into methane and CO 2 . Instead of substrate-level ATP production, methanogens conserve energy through a membrane-bound electron transport chain and flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB). Beyond the canonical modes of growth in methanogens, Methanosarcina acetivorans , a model acetotrophic methanogen, can conserve energy via direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET). Here, we review the metabolic pathways and electron transport processes involved in energy conservation during fermentative, respiratory, and DIET modes. Additionally, we discuss the role of FBEB in energy conservation in gut-associated Methanomassiliicoccus luminyensis . Finally, we discuss the potential roles of heterodisulfide reductase (Hdr) and the process of electron transfer during the reaction mechanism of electron-bifurcating HdrA2B2C2 complex in cytochrome-containing methanogens. Understanding the complex redox control mechanisms in these organisms has broader implications for sustainable energy and environmental management.

food.title: Sustainable 2-keto-L-gulonic acid biosynthesis via single-strain one-step fermentation
food.abstract: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is an essential antioxidant molecule that maintains normal physiological functions in humans. Currently, industrial production relies primarily on a three-strain, two-step fermentation process to produce 2-keto-L-gulonic acid (2-KLG), the direct precursor of vitamin C. 2-KLG is then converted to vitamin C through chemical lactonization. However, this process is limited by prolonged fermentation cycles, poor stability of the mixed-culture system, and complex process control. In recent years, engineered single-strain platforms capable of one-step 2-KLG biosynthesis have emerged as a promising strategy for more sustainable vitamin C production. Nevertheless, the efficiency of L-sorbose-to-2-KLG conversion in this system remains low, making it a major bottleneck to further improving 2-KLG production. This review summarizes recent advances on single-strain, one-step fermentation systems using Gluconobacter oxydans as the chassis strain. It focuses on strategies including genetic tool development, metabolic engineering, and key enzyme optimization. The review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical reference for optimizing and industrializing green biomanufacturing systems for vitamin C.

food.title: Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
food.abstract: Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Scope and approach To our knowledge, this study provides one of the first comparative critical analyses of the HACCP-based data governance frameworks of six major jurisdictions. We compare jurisdictions in which private actors play a relatively larger role in certification and implementation ('market-led': the United States, the European Union, Canada, and Japan) with those in which public institutions play a dominant role ('state-led': South Korea and China), positioned along a governance continuum in which all systems combine public and private functions, focusing on their capacity for real-time risk prediction, public-private data integration, and global interoperability. Key findings and conclusions The market-led systems examined tend to foster food safety culture but are affected by 'Data Silos' that limit actions to retrospective tracebacks. The state-led systems examined may enhance data integrity but can create a 'Data Island' paradox due to an over-reliance on automating isolated physico-chemical Critical Control Points. To overcome these limitations, we propose a conceptual framework for Full-Scale Digital Transformation (Full DX). Converging prerequisite programs, structured food safety culture assessment (e.g., Shapley-FAHP), and intentional threat mitigations (TACCP/VACCP) into an interoperable predictive network powered by ensemble machine learning could support a more resilient regulatory…

Cultivation of halophilic archaea in shallow subsurface Martian conditions has implications for extant life on Mars
food.abstract: The present-day Martian surface is generally considered inhospitable to life because of low atmospheric pressure, intense surface radiation, global desiccation, and oxidizing chemistry, which has been increasing since the late Noachian. However, shallow Martian subsurface regions where mineralogy has shown groundwater movement may include localized hypersaline environments capable of retaining liquid water and supporting microbial metabolism. Haloferax volcanii , a model halophilic archaeon, has previously been shown to survive under low-pressure Martian conditions (24 mbar) and to grow anaerobically supported by the Mars-relevant oxyanions nitrate and perchlorate under high-salinity conditions. Here, we investigated whether H. volcanii could actively grow under a combination of environmental and chemical conditions relevant to potentially habitable shallow subsurface Martian lacustrine settings. Cultures were incubated for 160 days under anoxic, CO₂-enriched, low-pressure conditions (24 mbar) in hypersaline liquid media supplemented with nitrate or perchlorate. Growth was observed in all low-pressure treatments and was confirmed by increases in optical density and biological reduction of nitrate and perchlorate. Scanning electron microscopy revealed extensive biofilm formation in low-pressure cultures, and Raman spectroscopy demonstrated the persistence of carotenoid biosignatures after prolonged incubation under Martian conditions. Liquid loss remained below 4% across all treatments, indicating long-term stability of hypersaline brines throughout the experiment. These results demonstrate for the first time that a halophilic archaeon is capable of active growth and metabolism under a Mars-relevant combination of low pressure, high salinity, anoxia, and oxidizing…

Elevated ozone reshapes wheat root-associated microbiomes through coordinated plant responses and rhizosphere environmental filtering
food.abstract: Elevated tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) threatens crop productivity, but how O 3 -induced changes in plant responses influence root-associated microbiomes remains unclear. We investigated the responses of microbial communities inhabiting the rhizosphere and root endosphere to elevated O 3 using four cultivars grown under ambient and 1.5-fold ambient O 3 in a field-based free-air O 3 -concentration enrichment (FACE) system. Plant traits, root-released organic carbon (ROC), rhizosphere properties, extracellular enzyme activities, and bacterial and fungal communities were jointly analyzed. Elevated O 3 reduced yield and root biomass, with cultivar-dependent changes in ROC. Elevated O 3 consistently increased rhizosphere pH and altered microbial resource allocation, increasing ecoenzymatic vector length by 4.1% and decreasing vector angle by 4.6%. Bacterial communities showed a stronger response than fungal taxonomic communities, particularly in the rhizosphere. However, variation partitioning indicated that soil properties, especially pH, rather than O 3 treatment alone, provided the strongest independent explanation for bacterial community variation. Fungal communities showed limited taxonomic turnover but exhibited shifts in predicted trophic guilds, including increased pathotroph- and saprotroph-associated groups and decreased symbiotroph-containing guilds under elevated O 3 . These results demonstrate that elevated O 3 reshapes the wheat root-associated microbiome through coordinated changes in plant performance, rhizosphere environmental filtering, and microbial functional strategies, highlighting the importance of plant-mediated processes in regulating belowground responses to atmospheric change. food.title: Survey among official veterinarians on condemnation criteria for broiler carcasses with external lesions and its potential use for computer vision applications
food.abstract: Post-mortem inspection (PMI) of broiler carcasses is essential for food safety and provides insights into animal health, welfare, and meat quality. Despite uniform legislation in Europe, condemnation criteria still vary among Official Veterinarians (OVs) and countries. This study aimed to collect data regarding condemnation criteria among European OVs conducting broiler PMI and to suggest how these could be used in the compliance audits of PMI computer vision systems (CVSs). An online survey was conducted among 155 OVs in 14 European countries. Respondents assessed 11 standardized image sets depicting common external lesions on broiler carcasses across seven severity levels. They were asked to indicate the point at which each lesion should render a carcass unfit for human consumption. A consensus criterion of ≥66% was applied to define a commonly agreed severity level that requires condemnation. Open-ended responses were analyzed to explore factors affecting PMI decisions. High consensus was achieved for clearly visible and advanced lesions, with most benchmarks established at moderate to high severity levels. Greater variability was found for borderline cases, particularly cellulitis and superficial dermatitis. Qualitative analysis of open-ended questions regarding PMI identified three main themes: 1) training needs; 2) lack of harmonization and support in decision-making; 3) OVs’ public health role and implications for broiler health and welfare. The findings emphasized the role of guidelines, experience, and working conditions in condemnation decisions. The collected PMI results may serve as references for harmonized, risk-based PMI and for evaluating CVS performance against OV assessments.

food.title: Scientific criteria and guidelines for identifying, reporting and interpreting omics data – transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics – in meat science research
food.abstract: Omics approaches offer a rapidly expanding and highly valuable means to study meat science research questions associated with on-farm and post-farm activities. To help ensure the reliability, reproducibility, and transparency of these methodologies, this paper provides practical recommendations for identifying, reporting and interpreting transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics studies in meat research with a focus on best practices regarding the experimental designs, data analysis, and interpretation of the results. Rather than restricting methodological innovation, these guidelines aim to establish recommended scientific criteria that enhance reproducibility, facilitate the integration of independently generated omics datasets through standardized reporting, compatible metadata and transparent analytical workflows among studies submitted to Meat Science journal. Although individual technologies continue to evolve, adherence to the key principles and criteria will substantially improve the scientific soundness and long-term impact of omics generated data applied to meat science research.

food.title: Occurrence of aflatoxins, ochratoxin A, and unauthorised synthetic dyes in bulk paprika from two provinces of Türkiye: Dietary exposure and health risk assessment
food.abstract: Paprika is susceptible to contamination by naturally occurring mycotoxins and economically motivated adulteration with illegal synthetic dyes, posing potential food safety concerns. This study investigated the occurrence of four aflatoxins (AFs), ochratoxin A (OTA), and 13 unauthorised synthetic dyes in 105 unbranded bulk paprika samples collected from retail spice shops in Türkiye using validated HPLC-FLD and LC-MS/MS methods. AFB 1 was the predominant mycotoxin, detected in 70.5% of samples, whereas OTA occurred in 26.7%. Regulatory exceedances for AFB 1 were limited, and no sample exceeded the European Union maximum level for OTA. Among the prohibited dyes analysed, Sudan I and Sudan IV were detected in 5.7% and 1% of samples, respectively. Under the upper-bound scenario, deterministic margin of exposure (MOE) values were 38,531 for AFB 1 and 1,578,678 for OTA. The probabilistic assessment yielded 5th percentile MOE values of 10,535 and 377,691 for AFB 1 and OTA, respectively. All reported MOE values exceeding the reference threshold of 10,000. These findings suggest a low level of public health concern for dietary exposure to AFs and OTA through paprika consumption, while highlighting the need for continued monitoring of mycotoxins and illegal dyes to ensure food safety and product authenticity.

food.title: Using DNA barcoding to uncover mislabelling in the flake trade along the supply chain across Southeast Australia
food.abstract: Seafood is a vital global resource, providing protein and essential nutrients to millions. However, ambiguous labelling practices, including the use of umbrella terms, can obscure origin and species composition. Such practices can conceal the trade of threatened species, undermining fisheries management and consumers’ ability to make informed choices. Like other generic names used internationally (e.g., ‘cação’, ‘rock salmon’), shark meat in Australia is commonly sold under the umbrella label of flake, with no mandatory regulations defining which species can be traded under this label. To identify mislabelling and assess the mix of different products, we used DNA barcoding of the Cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) to identify the species sold as flake across the entire supply chain (from fishers and wholesalers to fresh seafood and takeaway shops) in Southeast Australia. Sampling across different seasons also allowed insights into potential links to local fisheries. Of 423 samples sequenced successfully, 144 were identified to species level, and 279 to genus level, representing a total of 16 species and 12 genera. School shark Galeorhinus galeus , a critically endangered species, made up 20 % of identifications, with other notable species including smooth hammerhead and bull shark. Species composition varied across supply chain nodes with some species such as Elephantfish Callorhinchus sp. detected only in take-away products but no other supply chain nodes, which may suggest additional sources at later distribution stages. Overall, these findings highlight that ambiguity in umbrella labelling is widespread and increases towards the consumer end of the supply chain, underscoring the need for improved transparency and labelling.

food.title: Comparative evaluation of turbidity and impedance microbiology for rapid quantification of Bacillus cereus in skim milk under different temperatures, salt levels, and incubation times
food.abstract: Rapid quantification of Bacillus cereus in milk is critical because this organism can survive pasteurization, grow during chilled storage, and cause spoilage or foodborne illness. This study compares a microplate-based turbidimetric system (Bioscreen C o Pro™) with an automated impedance analyzer (BacTrac 4300) for enumerating B. cereus in skim milk across a factorial combination of four temperatures (10, 20, 30, and 37 °C), four sodium chloride levels (0.11, 0.8, 1.5, and 3.0% (w/v) NaCl), and two incubation times (24 and 72 h). Bacterial growth was monitored in parallel by plate counting, optical density at 600 nm (OD 600 nm ), and impedance measurements, and primary Baranyi–Roberts modeling was used to derive method-specific detection times (DTs). Method-specific calibration equations relating DTs to viable bacterial concentrations were established and subsequently used to estimate B. cereus populations in skim milk samples previously incubated under different temperature, salinity, and incubation time conditions. Both rapid methods showed strong linear relationships between DT and actual cell concentration (log 10 CFU/mL), but impedance-based predictions demonstrated better agreement with plate counts than turbidimetric predictions ( R 2 = 0.90 vs. 0.82; pooled RMSE = 0.657 vs. 1.153 log₁₀CFU/mL, respectively) and consistently yielded shorter DTs, particularly at higher temperatures and longer incubation times, while elevated NaCl and low temperature markedly delayed or prevented growth. These findings provide a systematic, plate-count-referenced comparison of turbidimetric and impedance-based quantification of B. cereus under the tested skim-milk conditions. food.title: Bacterial and fungal community dynamics in black pepper (Piper nigrum) across different processing plants using culture-based and amplicon sequencing approaches
food.abstract: Black pepper (Piper nigrum) is among the most commercially relevant spices worldwide, yet its microbial ecology throughout processing remains insufficiently understood, particularly in relation to food safety. Despite being a low-water-activity product, black pepper may harbor diverse bacterial and fungal communities, including spoilage microorganisms, mycotoxigenic fungi, and foodborne pathogens. In this study, we investigated the dynamics of bacterial and fungal communities along the black pepper processing chain in three distinct processing plants. A total of 154 samples were collected from processing plants A, B, and C in São Mateus, Espírito Santo, Brazil. Culture-dependent analyses included enumeration of aerobic mesophilic bacteria, Enterobacteriaceae, lactic acid bacteria, total fungi, and xerophilic fungi; fungal isolation and identification; and Salmonella detection and confirmation. Culture-independent profiling was performed by amplicon sequencing targeting the V3-V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene and the V9 region of the 18S rRNA gene. Microbial counts increased throughout processing, indicating that post-drying operations represent critical contamination points. Fungal isolation revealed genera of hygienic and toxicological relevance, including Aspergillus, Fusarium, Penicillium, and Cladosporium. Salmonella was detected in 14.3% of the samples, comprising nine serotypes, with the highest occurrence after drying. Amplicon sequencing identified 5 phyla and 85 genera in the fungal community, whereas for the bacterial community, 24 phyla and 475 genera were identified, with Ascomycota, Proteobacteria and Firmicutes predominating across samples. food.title: Antifungal effect of Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 on postharvest internal decay of chestnut and its potential antifungal mechanisms
food.abstract: Chestnut Inner Rot Disease (CIRD), a serious postharvest disease caused by multiple fungal pathogens, leads to substantial economic losses in the chestnut industry. Microbial biocontrol offers a safe and effective strategy. In this study, targeting four dominant CIRD pathogenic strains previously isolated, a bacterial strain identified as Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 was isolated from chestnut-cultivated soil. BLS-7 exhibited strong antifungal activity against Diaporthe phaseolorum, Colletotrichum siamense, Fusarium culmorum, and Lasiodiplodia theobromae, with inhibition rates of 84.51% to 96.89%. Moreover, it demonstrated broad-spectrum antagonism against 14 tested pathogenic fungi, all with inhibition rates exceeding 64%. In vivo assays further verified the significant biocontrol efficacy of BLS-7 across different chestnut varieties. Whole-genome sequencing analysis revealed that the BLS-7 genome harbors 13 gene clusters associated with secondary metabolite synthesis. Through headspace solid-phase microextraction combined with Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) of BLS-7 were analyzed, identifying hexyl butyrate as a candidate key inhibitory monomer. This compound inhibited three of the four CIRD pathogens by over 80% in vitro and all four in chestnut assays, with maximum inhibition rates of 82.95% and 75.3%, respectively. Both the VOCs and hexyl butyrate produced by BLS-7 suppressed mycelial growth and sporulation by disrupting hyphal morphology. VOCs and hexyl butyrate also restricted fungal spread on chestnuts and delayed fruit quality deterioration. This work proposes a fumigation-mediated VOC strategy using hexyl butyrate as a candidate key effector against multi-pathogen chestnut rot, offering a promising…

food.title: Biopesticide-associated Bacillus thuringiensis on retail fresh produce: occurrence, typing and implications for food-safety surveillance
food.abstract: Bacillus thuringiensis is one of the most widely used microbial biopesticides and is likely to gain further relevance in the transformation of agrifood systems. However, as a member of B. cereus sensu lato ( B. cereus s.l. ), B. thuringiensis may harbor enterotoxin genes associated with diarrheal illness, raising food-safety concerns about its presence on minimally processed fresh produce. This study aimed to generate a surveillance-oriented retail dataset on the prevalence and genetic diversity of B. thuringiensis on retail fresh produce. A total of 280 fresh produce samples, including leafy greens, vegetables, and fruits, were collected from a retail distribution center in Switzerland, and presumptive B. cereus s.l. was enumerated according to ISO 7932:2004 (limit of detection, 5 CFU/g). Presumptive B. cereus s.l. isolates were subjected to PCR-based profiling of enterotoxin genes, and B. thuringiensis -associated insecticidal toxin genes ( cry genes). Selected isolates were further characterized by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy for clustering, and a subset was analyzed by whole-genome sequencing for high-resolution comparison with commercially used biopesticide strains. B. thuringiensis was detected in 22% of produce samples and occurred at comparable frequencies across produce categories. Isolates predominantly showed biopesticide-associated profiles, and 20 out of 22 sequenced B. thuringiensis isolates showed close genomic relatedness to commercially used biopesticide strains. These findings provide a surveillance-relevant retail baseline for biopesticide-associated B. thuringiensis on fresh produce. The observed profiles are consistent with residues from B. thuringiensis -based biopesticides contributing to its occurrence at retail. Together,…

food.title: Effects of embryonic thermal manipulation and post-hatch synbiotic supplementation on growth performance, gut morphology, skeletal traits and caecal microbiota of broiler chickens under tropical conditions
authors: C. A. H. C. Ab Ghani
food.abstract: 1. This study investigated the effects of embryonic thermal manipulation and post-hatch synbiotic supplementation on growth performance, intestinal morphology, foot health, leg strength and tibial characteristics of broiler chickens reared in tropical conditions.2. A total of 840 fertile Ross 308 eggs were incubated at either the optimal temperature (37.5°C) or subjected to embryonic thermal manipulation (38.5°C from embryonic days (ED) 8 to 14). After hatch, chicks received either a basal diet or a basal diet supplemented with a synbiotic (1 g/kg) until 42 d of age.3. From d 21–28 all birds experienced an outbreak of leucocytozoonosis and received identical antiparasitic treatment, enabling comparisons of treatments under disease challenge.4. Embryonic thermal manipulation reduced hatchability (87.7 vs. 95.7%), starter feed intake and early body weight, but did not affect final body weight. Synbiotic supplementation improved overall feed conversion ratio. Under optimal incubation conditions, synbiotic supplementation increased body weight gain and duodenal villus height, whereas, following embryonic thermal manipulation, it increased tibial phosphorus content but reduced villus height.5. Neither embryonic thermal manipulation nor synbiotic supplementation affected gait score, latency-to-lie or caecal bacteria. Footpad dermatitis and hock burn scores increased only in synbiotic-supplemented broilers incubated at optimal temperature.6. Embryonic thermal manipulation altered the response to post-hatch synbiotic supplementation, shifting the benefits from enhanced intestinal morphology and growth performance to improved tibial mineralisation. These findings underscored the importance of incubation conditions when devising nutritional strategies for broiler production.

food.title: Pharmacokinetics and plasma protein binding of oxytetracycline in ducks ( Anas platyrhynchos ) following intravenous, intramuscular, subcutaneous and oral administration
food.abstract: 1. Tetracyclines are among the most widely used antibiotics in poultry, with oxytetracycline (OTC) playing a key role due to its routine administration via feed and water to treat susceptible bacterial infections. Despite its widespread clinical use, understanding of the pharmacokinetics of OTC in the genus Anas remains remarkably limited. The following study characterised the pharmacokinetic profile of OTC after intravenous (IV), intramuscular (IM), subcutaneous (SC) and oral administration in ducks (Anas platyrhynchos).2. A total of 24 ducks (six per group in a parallel study) were given OTC at a dose of 40 mg/kg via IV, IM, SC and oral routes. Blood samples were collected at various time points ranging from 0 min (control) to 96 h post-administration. The samples were examined by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and the pharmacokinetic parameters were assessed through non-compartmental analysis.3. Following IV administration, the volume of distribution (2.73 l/kg) suggested extensive tissue penetration. Elimination half-lives were 12.69 h (IM), 13.54 h (SC) and 12.62 h (oral), all slightly longer than after IV dosing (9.72 h) with no significant differences between extravascular routes. Bioavailability was high after parenteral administration (≈90–98%), suggesting near-complete absorption, whereas oral bioavailability was low (≈17%), indicating gastrointestinal absorption as the main limiting factor. Plasma protein binding was high (87–93%).4. Parenteral administration of OTC (40 mg/kg) in ducks can achieve effective exposure against pathogens with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) ≤0.5 µg/ml.

food.title: Effects of environmental enrichments applied to pasture areas on free-range laying hens: 1. Performance and egg quality
food.abstract: 1. This study assessed the effects of environmental range enrichments, bird age and their interactions on laying performance and egg quality from Lohmann Brown hens.2. In total, 900 hens (25 weeks old) were randomly divided into three groups (control, object [OE] and tree [TE] enrichment) with three pen replicates each (100 hens/pen). Each pen was a closed shelter with pasture access nearby. Variously rectangular, square, cylindrical and triangle shaped, red, orange and yellow-coloured boxes, pipes, buckets and structures were used for the OE group, whereas tall and broad-leaved plants and Thuja trees were used for the tree enrichment group.3. Laying performance and egg quality traits were measured at 25–32, 33–40, 41–48 and 49–56 weeks of age.4. Significant differences in egg production were found amongst all groups (p < 0.01) due to differences in mortality at the start of the experimental period (p <<0.001). There were no significant differences between treatments in hen-day egg production. Environmental enrichment significantly decreased the albumen index and affected dirty egg ratio, shell thickness (p < 0.01) and shell weight (p < 0.05). Shell weight showed an interaction between enrichment and age (p < 0.01).5. Age had a significant effect on all performance and egg quality traits (p < 0.05), with 48-week-old hens generating the highest egg mass and hen-day and hen-housed egg production levels (p < 0.01).6. Although environmental enrichment can potentially increase egg production slightly, TE and OE resulted in fewer clean eggs. However, positive effects on albumen and shell quality traits were evident in the OE group.

food.title: Effects of environmental enrichments applied to pasture areas on free-range laying hens: 2. Pasture use, behaviour and welfare
food.abstract: 1. This study assessed the effects of environmental enrichment on outdoor ranges for birds aged either 25, 36, 48 and 56 weeks on pasture use, behaviour and welfare of free-range laying hens. In total, 900 hens (25 weeks old) were randomly divided into three groups (control, object enrichment and tree enrichment) with three pens each (100 hens/pen). Each group was provided with a closed shelter and pasture range nearby.2. A control (CON) group of birds was maintained without any extra enrichment. Various rectangular, square, cylindrical and triangle shaped boxes, pipes, buckets and structures in yellow, red and orange colour were used for the ‘object’ (OBJ) enrichment treatment, whereas tall and broad-leaved plants and Thuja trees were used for the ‘tree’ (TREE) enrichment treatment.3. The use of total pasture area in hens was not different amongst enrichment treatment groups or bird age. While the proportion of OBJ hens using the inner zone of the pasture was higher (p < 0.01), CON and TREE hen groups were found more in the outer zone of the pasture (p < 0.01).4. Enrichment treatment and age did not affect blood heterophil, lymphocyte and heterophil/lymphocyte (H/L) ratio. Feeding, drinking, walking, foraging, resting/laying, perching, scratching/preening and pecking behaviours were not different between enrichment treatment groups. Hens exhibited more feeding, drinking, walking, foraging and less perching, scratching/preening and pecking behaviours with age (p < 0.01).5. There were no differences in feather condition, comb wounds, foot pad dermatitis, keel bone damage, duration of tonic immobility or induction number amongst the enrichment groups.
